# How good is the data? {#sec-data-quality}


::: {.cell}

:::


No administrative dataset is perfect, and this one combines three. This
chapter summarises how far the CARS data can be relied on, starting with how
its vehicle counts compare with DfT's official counts. The pipeline's
[Registration report](../reports/registration_report.md)
covers that comparison in full, by body type, age, fuel, engine size,
registration year and postcode area. The
[Data quality report](../reports/data_quality_report.md) has every other check.

## Comparison with DfT vehicle counts

DfT's vehicle licensing statistics count every vehicle on the DVLA register at
the end of each year, split into licensed (taxed) and SORN. The CARS data
counts vehicles that are tested. To compare like with like:

- **Count a vehicle in CARS only if it has another MOT later.** CARS carries a
  vehicle's postcode area forward for about two years after its last MOT
  (@sec-lifecycle), so a vehicle scrapped or exported after its last test stays
  in the located count after it has left DfT's. Dropping vehicles with no
  later MOT removes them. The registration report calls this the **MOT stock**.
- **Compare with DfT's licensed vehicles only.** SORN vehicles are not tested,
  and a SORN declaration does not need renewing, so DfT's SORN count includes
  vehicles that have long since been scrapped.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![CARS MOT stock (located, with an MOT in a later year) as a ratio of DfT's licensed vehicles of the same body type, all ages. Years after 2022 (shaded) are provisional, because a vehicle's last MOT cannot yet be told from the end of the data.](data-quality_files/figure-html/fig-dft-ratio-1.png){#fig-dft-ratio fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


On this basis the two sources agree closely. From 2014 to
2022, CARS has 1.00 to 1.03
times DfT's licensed cars, and 0.96 to
1.00 times its licensed vans. Comparing every located
vehicle with DfT's licensed plus SORN count instead gives a misleading
1.04 for cars and
0.60 for motorcycles in 2022.

**The last three years are provisional.** The pipeline cannot tell a vehicle
whose last MOT was in 2024 from one that is simply due again
after the data ends, so in 2023 to 2025 the stock count
drops vehicles that are still on the road. Use 2022 or earlier for
single-year comparisons.

**Motorcycles** match too once the comparison is like for like
(0.97 in 2022), but they are the
body type CARS covers least well:

- **SORN.** DfT's SORN motorcycles grew from
  746,761 in 2014 to
  1,521,447 in 2025, more than the
  licensed count. This is most of the apparent shortfall in the old
  comparison.
- **The 40-year exemption.** Vehicles 40 or more years old have not needed an
  MOT since May 2018. In 2022 DfT had
  140,337 licensed motorcycles of that age
  (10.3% of licensed motorcycles, against
  0.8% of cars); CARS has
  10,493.
- **Bikes that never take an MOT.** About one motorcycle in 9
  registered since 2012 never appears in the MOT data
  (88.5% of DfT's count at age one ever does), while for cars
  the MOT data holds at least as many as DfT counts at age one
  (102.8%). They are mostly mopeds and 125cc
  scooters from low-cost makes, road-registered enduro and trials bikes, and
  electric mopeds.
- **Taxed without an MOT, and seasonal SORN.** When the DVLA record was read,
  7.3% of taxed motorcycles aged 3 to 39 had no valid
  MOT, against 2.3% of cars, and
  13.3% of motorcycles still being tested were on SORN
  (cars 1.5%).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Cars, vans and motorcycles by age in 2022: the CARS MOT stock and DfT's licensed count. Age 40 includes all older vehicles.](data-quality_files/figure-html/fig-dft-age-1.png){#fig-dft-age fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


By age (@fig-dft-age), the sources agree well from 3 to about 39 years.
Vehicles under three have not had an MOT, so CARS holds only the ones known
from DVLA records. From 40, vehicles are exempt from the MOT and most drop out
of CARS.

Heavy goods vehicles, most buses and coaches, tractors, plant and mobility
scooters do not take the MOT test at all, so CARS holds them only through DVLA
records and does not reflect their numbers.

## Completeness of key fields


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

:::


| Field | Missing | Note |
|---|--:|---|
| Make (`make_final`) | 0.56% | |
| Model (`model_final`) | 4.27% | Mostly where the recorded model is a placeholder such as UNKNOWN |
| Body type | 3.14% | |
| Fuel (`fuel`) | 0% | "Other" for a small number |
| Engine size (`engine_cc`) | 0.87% | Mostly tractors and plant |
| CO~2~ (`co2`) | 26.14% | Mostly older vehicles, registered before CO~2~ was recorded |
| Euro standard (`euro_standard`) | 8.84% | Includes values assumed from the date. `euro_status` is never empty: a vehicle with no standard holds the reason (`pre_euro`, `no_schedule` or `no_date`) |
| Test class (`test_class`) | 5.9% | |
| First-use date | 0% | From DVSA for 82.3% of vehicles |

## Known issues

- **The final years are incomplete.** 2025 is a partial year, and the youngest
  vehicles are missing from the last three years (@sec-pitfalls).
- **Northern Ireland** vehicles are included, but the anonymised test class
  is not supplied for them, and testing there was disrupted in 2020.
- **Vehicles first registered between March and July 2017** had their first
  MOT delayed by the COVID-19 extension in 2020. About a quarter of them have
  no postcode area until 2020, so 2018 and 2019 undercount that cohort
  (@sec-meth-annualising).
- **2005** appears to be of lower quality than later years, and some CARS
  reports start comparisons in 2006.
- **DVLA records describing another vehicle.** Where a registration has moved
  between vehicles, the DVLA record may describe the wrong one. The pipeline
  detects the clear cases and does not use their values; some subtler cases
  will remain.
- **Make and model matching** is very good for common vehicles and weaker for
  rare ones, motorcycles and specialist vehicles. `model_confidence` and
  `model_method` show how each match was made.

:::
